subject: Re: EU/UK data transfer modules — confirmation & implementation steps
body:
From: Sarah Taylor <sarah.taylor@acme-health.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acme-health.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU/UK transfer clauses — module preference and evidence request

Hi Jonas,

Quick follow-up from legal on our side. We need Redwood to confirm which SCC module Redwood intends to execute for the standard EU->US (and UK->US) flows for Acme Health. Specifically:

- For Acme as Controller and Redwood as Processor, will Redwood execute Module Two (Controller -> Processor) in the DPA?
- For any downstream transfers (Redwood -> cloud infra / analytics vendors), will Redwood be using Module Three (Processor -> Processor) for those subprocessors?

Also: can you attach a short matrix that maps each data flow to the SCC module and include the draft execution clause we should insert into our DPA? Our procurement team needs it to complete the security intake.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — procurement is aiming for sign-off next week.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Taylor
Data Protection Lead | Acme Health
[Attachment: Acme-Checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

---
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Taylor <sarah.taylor@acme-health.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EU/UK transfer clauses — module preference and evidence request

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Internal summary and proposed approach below (copied to legal & privacy for final language).

Summary / recommendation (high level):
- Redwood will execute Module Two (Controller -> Processor) with Acme Health for the primary service flows where Acme is Controller and Redwood processes data on Acme's behalf.
- For downstream transfers where Redwood engages cloud infra or third-party analytics (those vendors acting as subprocessors), Redwood will rely on Module Three (Processor -> Processor) or equivalent contractual assurances between Redwood and those vendors and will list them in our subprocessor registry.
- We will include the standard UK Addendum where requested for UK-origin data.

Deliverables we will provide by EOD Friday:
- SCCs module-selection matrix (maps flow -> SCC module) [stub: SCCs-module-selection-matrix-20261118.xlsx]
- Draft DPA excerpt showing SCC execution clause and UK addendum reference [stub: Redwood-DPA-draft-20261118.pdf]
- Annex A (stubbed list of subprocessors and roles) [stub: Redwood-SCCs-Annex-A-stub.pdf]

Open items for your legal/procurement team:
- Confirm whether Acme requires Redwood to sign controller->controller language for any specific product features (unlikely for hosted API but flagging).
- If Acme insists on processor->controller Module Four for any reverse flows, let us know which particular flows so we can evaluate.

Marissa / Neha — can you confirm the implementation notes below and flag any redlines we should expect from Acme?

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, EMEA | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Sarah Taylor <sarah.taylor@acme-health.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EU/UK transfer clauses — module preference and evidence request

Hi all,

Legal confirm: recommended and standard approach below. Putting this on the record so procurement has language to consume.

1) Primary relationship (Acme Controller -> Redwood Processor)
- Module Two (Controller -> Processor) is the appropriate SCC module and Redwood will execute Module Two in the DPA.
- We will reference the EU SCCs 2021 set and attach the UK Addendum for UK-origin data.

2) Downstream subprocessors (Redwood -> Cloud / analytics vendors)
- Those flows are Processor -> Processor. Module Three governs P->P transfers. As a practical matter Redwood will ensure that subprocessors either:
  a) execute Module Three with Redwood, or
  b) have equivalent contractual safeguards (e.g., vendor SCCs / EU-approved mechanisms) plus documented security controls.
- Redwood will maintain a public subprocessor registry and provide Acme with the current list + evidence on request (SOC 2 reports / vendor contracts redacted as needed).

3) Implementation notes / redlines likely from customer:
- Customers sometimes ask Redwood to accept UK-specific signature or annex placement; we prefer to keep SCC execution referenced in the DPA and attach the SCCs/UK Addendum as annexes.
- Logging/access definitions: Acme may request narrower access/retention windows for logs — these are typically product settings (we can accommodate in Dedicated or Private deployments with configuration or contractual commitments).

4) Proposed DPA clause (high level text for insertion):
- "Customer (as Controller) and Redwood (as Processor) agree to execute the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module Two) as set out in Annex X to this DPA for transfers of personal data from the EEA/UK to Redwood's processing locations. Where Redwood transfers data to its subprocessors, such transfers shall be governed by Module Three or equivalent safeguards. The parties also agree to execute the UK Addendum where applicable."

Next steps I recommend:
- Jonas: send the three deliverables to Acme (matrix, DPA excerpt, Annex A).
- Acme: review and confirm Module Two is acceptable for Controller->Processor flows and indicate any specific subprocessors or flows they are concerned about.
- Legal teams: be available for a 30-min alignment call if Acme proposes deviations.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood-DPA-draft-20261118.pdf (PDF)]

Confirmation: Redwood will execute Module Two (Controller -> Processor) with Acme for the primary service relationship. For downstream subprocessors (cloud infra, analytics), Redwood will ensure Module Three (Processor -> Processor) is in place between Redwood and those vendors or otherwise documented equivalent safeguards; Redwood will share SOC 2 evidence for those vendors on request. We will include the UK Addendum for UK-origin data.

Attachments (stubs):
- Redwood-DPA-draft-20261118.pdf — includes proposed insertion (Annex X) where Module Two is executed and UK Addendum called out.
- SCCs-module-selection-matrix-20261118.xlsx — maps each high-level flow (API ingestion, KV-cache backups, logging to analytics) to Module Two or Module Three as appropriate.
- Redwood-SCCs-Annex-A-stub.pdf — preliminary subprocessor list + roles.

Suggested timeline:
- Thu 19 Nov: Acme legal review + request any redlines (we will prioritize).
- Fri 20 Nov: Short alignment call (15–30 min) if Acme proposes redlines; otherwise, final DPA signature window next week.

If you need a copy of our SOC 2 (redacted) or specific vendor contracts, Marissa can pull and share via secure link.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to close this out.

Best,
Jonas
